meta.description:
The mission of Army Community Service (ACS) is to strengthen our community and enhance mission readiness, retention, and adaptation to the military lifestyle by providing total force members, their families, and leadership with effective, measurable services. While we do not provide clinical counseling, we help prioritize concerns and identify the resources or new behaviors needed to navigate the client's situation. 
We are location in the Soldier Support Building to the far left entrance, 650 Monroe Ave., Room 126.
meta.references: All required documents can be found at the ACS SharePoint, Safety Folder: https://usaf.dps.mil/_layouts/15/sharepoint.aspx/onedrive
meta.jhaNotes:
OFFICE HAZARDS
Major causes of office injuries are falls, pushing/pulling, tripping and manual lifting. Personnel working in offices should keep file draws closed when not in use. Do not drape extension cords across walking areas or any other object that could be stepped on or cause a person to lose their balance. Avoid placing objects in high traffic areas and do not stand on chairs with wheels or wobbly desks or other unsuitable surfaces. Clean up spills immediately and post signs denoting wet floors. Remove obstructions from doorways and hallways.

ELECTRICAL SHOCK / EXTENSION CORDS
Before plugging a cord into the outlet, take a moment to look at the cord. The cord should be free from cracks, cuts or abrasions. If any defects in the cord are found, the cord needs to be replaced. Covering up the defect with electrical tape is not an approved fix. Notify your supervisor about the defected equipment. Electricity and water don’t mix.

HAZARDOUS CHEMICALS
When using cleaning supplies, do not mix different products (especially bleach and ammonia).  Open doors or turn on fans when using strong disinfecting sprays.  Use gloves when handling concentrated liquids or strong solutions.  Keep all items away from skin/eyes.

Air Force civilian personnel must complete a Form CA-1 and CA-2 (obtained from your supervisor) prior to seeking treatment at the base hospital for any work-related injury or illness (emergencies excepted).

All active-duty military personnel, Air Force civilian personnel, and Non-Appropriated Funds personnel, whether full-time or part-time, are authorized to use the hospital for emergency treatment.
meta.evacuationRoute: When directed, evacuate the building (taking your CAC) to a distance of at least 100 feet. Leave Bldg. 650 via front door and assemble in the secondary parking lot so all personnel may be accounted for by the senior ranking member.
meta.shelterInPlace:
1.“Sheltering-in-place” is in response to a chemical, biological or radiological contamination that may have been released into the environment.
2. Shelter-in-place areas in Army Community Service building 650 are designated with yellow signs. The ACS has pre-identified the Conference Room, Rm 11A as our shelter-in-place area.
3. When instructed to “shelter-in-place,” swiftly move to the Conference Room. Once inside, seal windows, doors, and ventilation systems using tape, plastic, and weather stripping to avoid a chemical disturbance.
meta.activeShooterMethods:
1. When instructed to “lockdown,” it is in response to an active shooter event. During an active shooter emergency, you will be asked to lock/barricade yourself in a room with no windows, if possible.
2. If a room with no windows is not available in the building, try to take cover or stay out of view from any potential threat.
3. The idea of a “lockdown” is to remain properly secured and out of the active shooter’s line of vision until the area is secure.
meta.adverseWeatherShelter: In case of severe weather and we need to shelter in place, directly move to the ACS Conference Room, Rm 6A.  Stay away from windows and falling debris.
meta.fireEquipmentNotes:
Fire Reporting: Activate fire alarm. Alarms are located next to main exit the other inside the kitchen by door. Shout FIRE FIRE FIRE! Evacuate the building then dial 911. (Note: if using your cell phone, state you are calling from base). State the emergency, give Bldg. address 650 Monroe Ave., name, rank and phone number. “As a last resort” fight the fire with a fire extinguisher.
Review map to see where are the emergency equipment's located for ACS.
meta.safetyBoardLocation: Personnel should review the safety board once a month to ensure they are aware of all current safety policies. The safety bulletin board is located in the back wall in Staff Room 8A.
meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
Annual crash data for the local area can be acquired at http://www.511virginia.org/

All personnel will obey posted speed limits on and off-base.
meta.trafficContacts: We do not have a Unit Motorcycle Rep because our squadron is all civilians.
meta.documentNotes: Training documents will be reviewed annually and the safety monitor will log the reviewed material via AF 55.

moduleReferences.title: Reporting Unsafe Equipment, Conditions, or Procedures
Mishap, Occupational Injury, and Illness Reporting

selectedModules.title: Ladder Safety
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 7
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers to inspect ladders before use, maintain three points of contact, set ladders on stable surfaces, and avoid overreaching or using damaged ladders.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide hands-on ladder safety training at first assignment, including local storage, damaged-tag procedures, and fall prevention expectations.

selectedModules.title: Active Shooter Response
selectedModules.reference: Installation emergency management guidance / local procedures
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Brief personnel on how to recognize an active shooter event, how to summon help, and how to apply local run-hide-fight guidance based on the facility layout.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local emergency response procedures, shelter locations, and mass notification methods applicable to the duty location.

selectedModules.title: Government Vehicle / Utility Vehicle Use
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train vehicle operators on seat belts, speed limits, local traffic hazards, spotter use while backing, and restrictions on electronic device use while driving.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Brief operators on unit-specific government vehicle training requirements, local route restrictions, low-speed vehicle rules, and documentation of qualification.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Concepts

selectedModules.title: Manual Lifting and Material Handling
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 20
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers on proper lifting techniques, team lifting, load assessment, and use of lifting aids to reduce musculoskeletal injury risk.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide verbal and written guidance on manual lifting, lifting devices, and local reporting actions for strain or overexertion symptoms.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Ergonomics and Material Handling Concepts

selectedModules.title: Fire Protection and Prevention
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards; local fire prevention plan
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on fire hazards, reporting procedures, extinguisher locations, evacuation routes, pull stations, and local emergency response actions.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the JSTO and local fire prevention plan to brief workers on work-center fire hazards, alarm reporting, extinguisher use, and evacuation accountability.

selectedModules.title: Hazard Communication
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on hazardous chemicals in their work area, labeling systems, safety data sheets, and the measures they can take to protect themselves during normal operations and foreseeable emergencies.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide HazCom training upon initial assignment, whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced, and when new tasks expose workers to different hazardous materials. Ensure workers know how to access local SDS information and labeling guidance.

selectedModules.title: Electrical & Office Appliance Safety
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Ch. 10 & 16; CE-approved appliances only, direct wall-outlet connection for high-draw units, no daisy-chaining
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Describe the unit-specific hazard, certification, or recurring training requirement that applies to this work center.

selectedModules.notes: Use of shredders, laminators, microwaves, space heaters, and conference audiovisual racks.  Electrical shock, trip hazards, fire hazards from daisy-chained surge protectors or unapproved space heaters.
